<action type="say">
Given what you described—recent card use, regular paycheck deposits, and that it used to show in this same profile—this almost certainly sounds like a visibility/linking issue in online banking, not that the checking account disappeared.

I don’t have the ability to “discover” or re-link hidden accounts beyond what’s listed for your profile, but here’s the fastest way to handle it:

1) Quick things to check yourself
- Log out and back in, and if your bank has both:
  - Check both “Accounts” and any “Card” or “Wallet” sections.
  - Look for filters like “Hide closed accounts” / “Show only active accounts” / “Show linked accounts only.”
  - If there’s a “Profile” → “Account linking” or “Account access” area, see if the checking account is listed but unchecked/hidden.

2) When you contact support (phone or in-branch)
Tell them something very close to this:

> “My main checking account, the one my paycheck is deposited into and that I used for a grocery purchase a few days ago, is no longer visible in my online banking profile. I used to see it in this same login. Can you:
> 1) Confirm that the checking account is open and active;  
> 2) Confirm that my direct deposit is still going there; and  
> 3) Re-link or restore that checking account so it shows up again under this online profile?”

If they ask for more detail, mention:
- You don’t remember the nickname or last 4 digits.
- It’s your primary payroll account and was used for a grocery transaction a few days ago.
- You have other accounts visible (auto loan, holiday savings, travel rewards credit card), but this checking is missing.

3) If you urgently need the balance before they fix it
Possible paths (depending on what your bank offers):
- Call support and ask: “Can you tell me the current available balance on the checking account that my payroll from [employer name, if you’re comfortable] goes into?”
- Use an ATM with the debit card tied to that checking—most will show the available balance when you check “Balance inquiry.”
- If your transaction history is still visible anywhere (e.g., card activity screen), you may estimate from the last known balance + recent transactions, but confirming with the bank is safer.

If you tell me which bank this is (and whether you’re on web or mobile), I can tailor the exact menu paths/wording for their app and their typical customer support options so you can get this fixed as quickly as possible. </action>

<action type="say">
Under this login I can only see the three accounts already listed, so I can’t directly read the hidden checking balance. To get today’s exact balance without going to an ATM or branch, you’ll need to contact Bank of New England support via the app or by phone and have them (1) tell you the balance and (2) fix the visibility issue.

Here’s the fastest way to do that from the mobile app:

1) Find support/contact inside the app
On Bank of New England’s app, look for one of these (usually in the bottom navigation or in a main menu ☰ icon):
- “Contact Us”
- “Help & Support”
- “Message Center” or “Secure Messages”
- A “Chat” or “Support” bubble icon

Tap that and choose either:
- “Call Us” (fastest), or  
- “Send a Secure Message” / “Chat with an agent”.

2) What to say to get your balance right now
If you call or chat, you can say almost exactly this:

> “I’m logged into my Bank of New England mobile app. My main checking account — the one my paycheck goes into and that I used for a grocery purchase a few days ago — is no longer visible in my accounts list.  
>  
> I need two things:  
> 1) Please tell me the current AVAILABLE balance on that checking account today.  
> 2) Please re-link or restore that checking account so it appears again in this online profile.”

If they ask for details (since you don’t know the digits or nickname), you can add:
- “It’s my primary payroll account; my paycheck from [employer name, if comfortable] goes there.”
- “My other accounts showing in the app are: Auto Loan 2022, Holiday Savings, and Travel Rewards credit card. The checking tied to my debit card and paycheck is missing.”

They’ll then:
- Authenticate you (security questions, text code, etc.), and  
- Be able to pull up all accounts under your customer profile—even ones that aren’t visible in the app—and read the balance to you.

3) If you don’t see a support option in the app
- Scroll to the very bottom of the “Accounts” or “More/Settings” screen; banks often list a phone number or “Contact” link there.
- If still nothing obvious, search “Bank of New England customer service phone” in your browser, call that number, and use the same script above. When the automated system asks what you’re calling about, say “checking account balance” or “representative.”

Once you’ve spoken with them and have the balance, tell me what they said and I can help you reconcile it with your recent activity (paycheck + grocery + other transactions) so everything makes sense.</action>
